title: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)
body: A pre-trained encoder-only transformer model that learns bidirectional representations by masking random tokens and predicting them. Used for classification, NER, and question-answering tasks. Introduced by Google in 2018.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers

title: GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer)
body: A decoder-only transformer model that generates text autoregressively, predicting the next token based on previous tokens. Powers systems like ChatGPT and GPT-4. Introduced by OpenAI with versions 1, 2, 3, and 4.

metadata.source_name: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

title: Fine-tuning
body: The process of adapting a pre-trained model to a new task by training it on task-specific data. Typically involves unfreezing some or all layers and using a small learning rate to avoid catastrophic forgetting.

title: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)
body: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique that freezes pre-trained weights and adds trainable low-rank decomposition matrices to model weights. Reduces memory and compute requirements while maintaining performance.

metadata.source_name: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

title: Prompt Tuning
body: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique that learns a set of continuous prompt embeddings prepended to input text, without modifying pre-trained model weights. Similar to prefix tuning.

metadata.source_name: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning

title: Inference Optimization
body: Techniques to reduce latency and memory footprint during model inference, including quantization, knowledge distillation, pruning, KV caching, and batching. Critical for production deployment at scale.

title: Quantization
body: Reducing model precision (e.g., from float32 to int8) to decrease memory usage and increase inference speed. Quantization-aware training accounts for quantization during training. Post-training quantization applies it after training.

metadata.source_name: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic Only Inference

title: KV Caching
body: A technique in transformer inference where past key-value pairs are cached to avoid recomputation. During autoregressive generation, only new tokens are computed; previous tokens' KVs are reused. Dramatically reduces inference latency.

title: Self-Attention
body: A mechanism allowing each token to attend to all other tokens in a sequence, computing a weighted sum of values based on similarity (via dot products of queries and keys). Core building block of transformers.

title: Multi-Head Attention
body: An extension of self-attention where attention is computed in parallel across multiple 'heads', each attending to different parts of the sequence. Results are concatenated and projected. Enables learning diverse attention patterns.

title: Tokenization
body: The process of breaking text into smaller units (tokens) that a model can process. Methods include character-level, word-level, and subword tokenization (BPE, WordPiece). Affects model vocabulary size and sequence length.

title: Collaborative Filtering
body: A recommendation technique that finds user-item patterns by analyzing user-item interactions (ratings, clicks, purchases). Assumes users with similar preferences will like similar items. Methods include user-user and item-item similarity.

title: Matrix Factorization
body: A collaborative filtering technique that decomposes a user-item interaction matrix into lower-rank user and item factor matrices. Each user and item has a latent vector; predictions come from dot products of these vectors.

metadata.source_name: Matrix Factorization Techniques for Recommender Systems

title: Content-Based Recommendation
body: A recommendation technique that recommends items similar to those the user has liked before, based on item features or attributes (genre, author, tags). Uses similarity metrics like cosine similarity on feature vectors.

title: Hybrid Recommendation
body: A recommendation approach combining multiple techniques (collaborative filtering, content-based, knowledge-based) to leverage strengths of each. Can improve coverage, handle cold-start better, and provide diverse recommendations.

metadata.source_name: Hybrid Recommender Systems: A Systematic Literature Review

title: Embeddings
body: Dense vector representations of entities (users, items, words) in a low-dimensional continuous space. Similar entities have vectors close in space. Used in both LLMs (word embeddings) and recommendation systems (user/item embeddings).

title: Ranking (in Recommendation Systems)
body: The second stage of many recommendation systems where candidates (retrieved by a retriever) are scored and ranked. Ranking models are often more complex and slower than retrievers, applied to smaller candidate sets to balance accuracy and latency.

metadata.source_name: Learning to Rank for Information Retrieval

title: Cold-Start Problem
body: A challenge in recommendation systems where new users or items have little interaction history. Solutions include content-based approaches, transfer learning, hybrid methods, or explicit feature collection.

title: Diversity in Recommendations
body: A goal in recommendation systems to provide varied recommendations, avoiding over-concentration on a few popular items. Balances accuracy (relevance) with coverage and serendipity. Achieved through re-ranking or diverse retrieval.

metadata.source_name: The Exposure-Diversity Trade-off in Search and Recommendation Systems

title: Feedback Loop (in Recommendation Systems)
body: A cycle where system recommendations influence user behavior, which generates new training data, which can reinforce or shift the system's recommendations. Can lead to filter bubbles but also enables online learning and adaptation.

metadata.source_name: The Feedback Loops Problem in Recommender Systems

title: CTR (Click-Through Rate)
body: The ratio of users who click on a recommendation to the total number of users who see it. Common metric for evaluating recommendation systems in ads and content feeds. Higher CTR indicates relevance and engagement.

title: Personalization at Scale
body: Delivering personalized recommendations to millions of users in real-time. Requires efficient architectures (two-tower models, retrieval-ranking pipelines), feature stores, and online serving infrastructure with latency constraints.

metadata.source_name: YouTube Recommendations at Scale: How to Deal with Billions of Items

title: Feature Store
body: Infrastructure for managing, versioning, and serving features (derived attributes) to ML models at training and serving time. Enables consistent feature definitions, reduces engineering overhead, and supports real-time feature updates.

title: Two-Tower Architecture (in Recommendation Systems)
body: An efficient recommendation architecture with separate embedding towers for users and items, trained end-to-end. User and item embeddings are computed independently and combined (dot product) for prediction. Used by YouTube, Meta, Airbnb.

title: Learning to Rank
body: A machine learning approach to ranking where models learn to score and order items based on features and training signals. Used in recommendation systems, search, and ads ranking. Balances multiple objectives (relevance, diversity, freshness).

metadata.source_name: Learning to Rank for Information Retrieval
